newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rate rise may be studied - LDP official quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan rate rise may be studied - LDP official quoted.

text.p: A senior official of the Liberal Democratic Party was quoted by a U.S. news agency as saying on Monday that a rise in Japan's official discount rate will probably be considered after general elections.

Shizuka Kamei, head of the LDP's press office, was quoted as saying at a seminar that a rise in the discount rate would be aimed at pushing up interest rates on savings. Japan's discount rate has been at a historic low of 0.5 percent since September last year. "The super low interest rate of 0.5 percent has not necessarily brought about favourable effects on the economy," he said.
"Low interest rates have benefited financial institutions, and have led to a drop in consumption," Kamei said.
The LDP is the biggest member of a three-party ruling coalition. Elections for the Lower House are set for October 20.
A spokesman for the Bank of Japan said the BOJ does not comment on media reports on changes in the discount rate.
Separately, Ichiro Ozawa, head of Japan's main opposition party Shinshinto, said on Monday that the country's interest rate levels must be corrected.
He said during a debate of heads of political parties ahead of the elections that unfavourable effects of low interest rates were spreading.
"Interest rate levels could be naturally adjusted as the the economy is activated. Interest rate levels must be corrected," he said.
He had been asked if low rates were affecting lives of people dependent on interest rate income.
The Bank of Japan's official discount rate has been at a record low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.
